summary: Recorded media that resells on eBay: out-of-print anime on disc, boutique restoration labels (Criterion, Scream Factory, Arrow, Vinegar Syndrome), discontinued Disney video, out-of-print TV box sets, collectible vinyl, CDs with real scarcity, laserdisc. Books are NOT here - they are covered by 'Specialty books and manuals' in lightweight_collectibles. Bulk lots are deliberately NOT here: the app's per-item price filter handles them, and a BOLO badge on one lot in eleven carries no information.
field_workflow: Discs: the case is worth nothing, the disc face and the paper insert are everything. Ask for a photo of the disc if the listing shows only the spine.
Box sets: confirm the count. 'Complete series' missing one disc drops to parts value.
Anime: the value is in the LABEL and whether it is still printed. Funimation/Geneon/ADV sets that went out of print are the money; a current Crunchyroll reprint is not.
Vinyl: matrix / runout etchings in the dead wax identify a first pressing. Ring wear on the sleeve caps the grade regardless of the disc.
CDs: a Japanese pressing keeps its OBI strip - without it a $60 CD is a $6 CD.
Bulk lots: count the pieces and divide. Under ~40 cents an item a mixed lot is worth taking on volume alone; above that it has to be the titles.
Region codes: a PAL or Region 2 disc will not play on an ordinary US player. It still sells, but to a smaller audience - discount it.
skip_list: Common studio catalogue DVD (Sony/Universal/Warner reprints, pennies each)
Ex-rental / library disc with case stickers and security tape
Reader's Digest condensed books and box sets
Damaged or missing OBI on a Japanese CD sold at OBI prices
Empty cases, sleeves and disc storage
Full-season network TV on VHS (near-zero demand)

era_markers: Geneon and ADV Films both shut down (2007-2009) - anything they pressed is finite
Funimation 'S.A.V.E.' reissues are the cheap version; the original thinpak sets are the money
Aniplex US limited editions are printed once, in small numbers
brands.notes: The highest-value disc category by a distance, and the one most often mispriced in a mixed lot because the label means nothing to a general seller.

era_markers: Spine number on the case edge - collectors buy by spine
Out-of-print spines (licence expired) are the ones that move
brands.notes: Steady rather than spectacular. Reliable enough that a Criterion spine in a mixed lot usually covers the whole lot.

era_markers: Limited pressing counts printed on the slipcover (e.g. '/3000')
The slipcover IS the value - a naked case is worth a fraction
brands.notes: Horror and cult restorations. Small print runs, dedicated buyers, and general sellers never recognise the label.

era_markers: Walt Disney Treasures tins are numbered and were made once
Song of the South was never released in the US - imports and bootlegs both circulate, so verify
brands.notes: Black Diamond VHS is the most over-hyped item in resale - real prices are modest. The numbered Treasures tins are the genuine money here.

era_markers: Music-licence expiry is what kills a reprint, so shows built on licensed music stay scarce
brands.notes: Heavy for the money - check the postage before bidding. A complete series missing a disc is worth parts value only.

era_markers: Runout / dead-wax etchings identify the pressing - the sleeve alone never does
Deep-groove labels and mono pressings date a jazz record to the first run
brands.notes: Grade honestly: buyers of records at this level return anything graded optimistically. Ring wear caps the price whatever the disc looks like.

era_markers: Longbox packaging dates a CD to 1986-1992
A Japanese pressing without its OBI strip loses most of its premium
brands.notes: Ordinary used CDs are close to worthless individually - this entry is only about the pressings that are not ordinary. Bulk CDs belong under the media-lot entry instead.

era_markers: Criterion's laserdiscs carried commentary tracks that never moved to DVD - that is the whole demand
brands.notes: Heavy, fragile and mostly worthless except for the handful of titles with exclusive extras. Check the title before the format.

platform_notes.eBay: Sold-listings filter is essential here - asking prices on discs are fantasy. Media Mail makes the postage workable on anything heavy.
platform_notes.Discogs: Better than eBay for vinyl and for CDs with pressing-level detail. Buyers expect accurate grading and will return anything optimistic.
platform_notes.Mercari: Works for anime and boutique discs; smaller audience, faster sales, lower ceiling.
